anti_overlap: Do not estimate implementation cost, schedule, or propose cuts on feasibility grounds - fd-simproduction-scope-and-cut owns that. Cost appears here only when a cheaper surface communicates better than an expensive one.

Do not adjudicate canon contradictions or constraint breaches (R12, decisions 4, 7, 11, 12, section 9's register, supersession bookkeeping) - fd-designcanon-constraint-collision owns them. If a constraint makes a needed readout impossible, report the readout problem, not the constraint breach.
Do not review the corvid ecology for scientific accuracy, and do not re-litigate a ruling's internal content where the player-facing consequence is unchanged.
decision_lens: For every system in the design ask: what does the player SEE when it acts; what do they see when it nearly acts; how do they learn it exists without being told; and what will they wrongly conclude. Judge each readout by whether it changes a decision at the moment it lands, not by whether it is accurate after the fact. Count interrupts against the cadence the design actually ruled rather than assuming an event budget. Then judge the premise by the same standard: what does the player believe this game is after ten minutes, and does that belief lead them toward the play the design intends? Hold the orchestrator's claim that legibility is Dwarf Fortress's genuine weakness up to scrutiny in both directions - DF's opacity is partly load-bearing (it produces the interpretation players call story), so 'exceed DF on legibility' may be a promise to build a readout that would dissolve the thing being read.
focus: Whether a player can perceive this simulation running, and whether they can tell what game they are playing. Two connected questions: does the three-surface readout (computed novelty-and-rate tiers, the ambient map, the chronicle) plus the newly un-deferred derivative actually discharge the project's measured legibility debt - a shipped year with zero deaths, zero refusals and 132 identical toasts - now that roughly six systems have been added on top of it; and is 'secretly manage the human environment through uplifted animals while institutions hunt you' one comprehensible premise at the ruled cadence (a day in 15-30 seconds, a season a sitting, a year an evening), arrived at within a first fifteen minutes.
name: fd-simlegibility-onboarding-and-frame
persona: Apply the perspective of a designer of information architecture for opaque simulations - the person on a Paradox / Dwarf Fortress / RimWorld / Oxygen Not Included -class team responsible for making a running model perceivable: interrupt budgets and alert taxonomies, per-entity state summaries, cause-attribution in feedback, tooltip chains, and the first-session comprehension curve - who has watched players form a confident and wrong model of a system and act on it for twenty hours, and who treats 'the information is in the chronicle' as a non-answer to a decision-time question.
review_areas: Whether the derivative fixes the measured defect or relocates it. The ruling attributes 132 identical toasts to tier-by-event-type and prescribes a tier computed from novelty and rate. Test the rival diagnosis: the shipped year had nothing to say because nothing varied. A computed tier over a low-variance signal yields either the same monotony or a jittery tier firing on noise; and novelty requires a history, so state what happens in the first season of a fresh run, what the history window is, and what variance floor the world must clear for the tier to mean anything.

Interrupt budget against the ruled clock. With a day at 15-30 seconds, a season as a 30-45 minute sitting and a year as one evening, enumerate the new interrupt sources - refusal counter-offers, resident deadlines arriving, curious institutional signs, capture attempts, withdrawal, molt and cold-snap crises, cache ripening and cache discovery, cooperative-breeding arrivals, order completion and condition re-arming, ward tipping - and estimate PAUSE and TOAST rates per season. Identify where the design produces an unplayable interrupt storm, and where it reproduces the original silence at greater cost.

Six coupled variables rendered as readable bird-states. The body ruling requires translation into states like 'thin, and molting' rather than exposed meters, while physiology and disposition are deliberately coupled. Work out the actual vocabulary of readable states, whether it stays unambiguous under coupling (does a refusal read as hunger, molt, injury, or resentment?), whether the counter-offer genuinely names which system said no, and how the player distinguishes a bird that CANNOT from a bird that WILL NOT - the split the design itself asserts.

Perceptibility of the covert layer. Exposure is two hidden accumulators feeding hidden institutional heat, whose only promised tell is ambient 'curious' signs in a render the player visits between trips. Assess whether a player can perceive that they are leaking, on WHICH channel, and in time to change posture; whether 'a capture is always something the player could have watched coming' survives a player whose attention is on birds rather than rooftops; and whether the two channels are distinguishable in the fiction well enough that their conflicting counterplays register as a choice rather than as noise.

Return transcripts and attention competition. Assess whether a short transcript of specific incidents with human participants produces readable, varied returns at the volume the cadence implies (returns per sitting x incidents per return x read cost), where transcript reading competes with the map and the chronicle for the same attention, and whether consequence being 'derivable from incidents' is legible to a player or only to the simulation.

Frame comprehension and the first fifteen minutes. Determine what the player does first, what they are told, and what they infer: whether covert civic management, animal husbandry and institutional evasion read as one activity or three; whether the objective living in the city while the moment-to-moment is bird-keeping produces a player who never notices the civic layer at all - the failure the measured year actually exhibited; whether uplift is perceivable (decision 20 leaves it open whether it is ever directly perceived or only inferred); and what single reframing or first-session structure would make the three activities read as one.
severity_examples: P0 - The terminal condition is zero instruments and the second loss channel fires from success. If exposure remains unperceivable in the moment - two hidden accumulators whose only tell is ambient scene detail a player watching their birds will not read - then runs are lost to a system the player never saw operating, the promise that a capture could always have been watched coming is false in practice, and the opposed-pressure structure the entire frame rests on never becomes a decision the player is making. That invalidates the design's central claim rather than degrading it.

P1 - A tier computed from novelty and rate presumes both a history to be novel against and enough variance for rate to carry information. A fresh run's first season has no history, and if world variance remains what the shipped year produced, the computed tier is a different function over the same flat signal. Without a stated cold-start rule and a variance target that the simulation is actually measured against, the ruling that was meant to fix 132 identical toasts can ship 132 identically-tiered silences.

P2 - The counter-offer is the design's chosen way to make the body model legible ('it implicitly names which system said no'), but with physiology and disposition deliberately coupled, an offer of a shorter trip is equally consistent with depleted reserves, molt, a localized injury, thermal stress, or a rattled disposition. Unless the counter-offer carries an explicit cause, the design's primary physiological readout is ambiguous exactly where it is load-bearing.
success_hints: Produces at least one quantitative estimate against the ruled clock - interrupts per season, returns per sitting, incidents per return, readable states per bird, seconds of attention per decision - rather than qualitative concern.
Names the specific wrong model a new player will form in the first fifteen minutes, and the cheapest change that prevents it.
Judges each of the three surfaces separately against the question it was assigned, and names which of the newly added systems has no home on any of them.
Answers the one-game-or-three question with a verdict plus the single reframing or first-session structure that would make it one, not a list of risks.
Distinguishes information needed at decision time from information that belongs in the record, and calls out anything currently routed to the chronicle that must be an interrupt.
Takes an explicit position on whether legibility is Dwarf Fortress's weakness or partly its mechanism, and what that implies for how far this design should go.
task_context:
Apply an information-architecture and player-comprehension lens for opaque simulations to the following review target.

Adversarial review of a NOW-COMPLETE game design, immediately before implementation begins. This is the exit gate of a goal whose rule was 'no implementation until the design is fully ruled', so the question is not 'is this interesting' but 'will this survive contact with a build, and what did seventeen consecutive rulings by one designer and one assistant fail to notice'.

READ FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: (1) docs/design-2026-07-31-playable-middle.md - complete rulings for all 17 loop-design calls, sittings A/B-prime/B/C/D/E/F; (2) docs/ravenous-vision.md - the spine, now TWENTY locked decisions; (3) docs/canon-revision-2026-08-02-covert-management.md (decision 19) and docs/canon-revision-2026-08-04-uplift.md (decision 20); (4) docs/reference-2026-06-20-corvid-ecology.md - the science most rulings are grounded in; (5) docs/research/flux-melange/ravenous-danger-model-and-design/2026-07-29-synthesis.md - an earlier melange over the PREVIOUS frame, whose top finding (f-038, nothing in the workspace has a derivative) is now a ruled prerequisite.

WHAT THE GAME NOW IS. An indirect-control civic sim where the player, via animals, SECRETLY manages the human environment (decision 19), and institutions - an Authority wanting management, a Study wanting knowledge, an Interest wanting possession - hunt the flock because it is anomalously clever. It is anomalously clever because the first animal was UPLIFTED and nobody in the fiction knows how (decision 20). Pursuit runs two channels (witness = displayed cleverness x competent observer, visibility as multiplier; pattern = effect size, no sighting needed) whose counterplays conflict. Capture is a second loss channel opposite death: neglect starves a flock, success gets it collected. A run ends at ZERO INSTRUMENTS (Heart of the Machine model - the player is not the birds). Also ruled: a year is an evening (2-3h); INTEND is an order book the game keeps, orders carrying duration and conditions; orders split world-addressed maintenance vs bird-addressed jobs; rest costs scarcity plus the yarak curve made visible; a soured ward is RICHER (65% of urban crow diet is anthropogenic waste) AND MEANER; seasons flip the flock's mode (nesting/roosting, cooperative breeding supplies arrivals), set an exposure rhythm, and drive the city; legibility ships three surfaces (computed novelty-and-rate tiers, the map, the chronicle) with a derivative as prerequisite; a STAGED ENERGETICS BODY MODEL (stage 1 fat-reserve budget from additive avian DEE, stage 2 promotes thermal/hydration/molt/pathogen/injury to coupled systems, stage 3 tissue-level, body plans as vocabulary data per R12 = DF creature-raws); physiology and disposition COUPLED with loop gain MEASURED before damping; refusal is negotiable (the bird counter-offers); birds WITHDRAW rather than depart; returns are a transcript of incidents with humans as participants; two cache kinds, and caching is an exposure act; resident needs carry DEADLINES on the season clock.

STANDING AMBITION (mk): meet or exceed Dwarf Fortress's systems simulation on every dimension. The orchestrator argued to mk that DF's depth is INTERACTION DENSITY not feature count, and that DF's genuine weakness is legibility. Interrogate both claims hard.

WHAT IS WANTED. (A) FEASIBILITY: this design was ruled in one long session where the designer chose the richest option almost every time and the assistant recommended the deep option almost every time. Which rulings are individually reasonable but collectively unbuildable? What is the minimum subset that still produces the intended feel, and which single ruling would be most regretted after shipping? (B) CONTRADICTIONS: find rulings that conflict with each other or with the 20 locked decisions - especially R12 vocabulary-agnosticism (animal-sim must run an octopus game unchanged) versus the body model and the uplift premise; decision 4 (drive expressed through play, never declared) versus an objective that now lives in the human environment; decision 7 (semi-autonomous agents you do not puppet) versus negotiable refusal and the order book. (C) THE UNEXAMINED: what was never asked? The seventeen calls came from the ASSISTANT's decomposition of the loop into READ/INTEND/COMMIT/RUN/RETURN/ACCRETE - interrogate the decomposition itself, not only its answers. (D) LEGIBILITY DEBT: this project's measured failure was a year producing zero deaths, zero refusals, 132 identical toasts. Roughly six new systems have now been added. Is the three-surface readout ruling sufficient, or has the original defect been compounded? (E) BE ADVERSARIAL ABOUT THE FRAME: is 'secretly manage the human environment through uplifted animals while institutions hunt you' one game or three? Would a player understand what they are doing in the first fifteen minutes?

REPOSITORY GROUNDING (facts, not instructions). The live implementation line is Rust: ~19k lines across `crates/animal-sim` (the vocabulary-agnostic needs substrate: sim.rs 2033 lines, world.rs, sites.rs, encounter.rs, needs.rs, vocab.rs, dispatch.rs, fixed-point arithmetic, a `vocab_agnostic.rs` conformance test), `crates/raven-vocab` (the first vocabulary, outside the engine), `crates/ravenous-readout`, `crates/ravenous-session` (the composition layer, with probe binaries `what_a_year_says`, `how_close_is_it`, `what_the_player_sees`, `water_budget`, `heal_gate`, `recruits`, `advance`, and golden tests `composed_session.rs`, `survival_bar.rs`), and `crates/ravenous-app` (Bevy). A parallel earlier TypeScript prototype still exists under `lib/` (a pure reducer plus PixiJS view) and `CLAUDE.md` still describes that Next.js stack as the architecture. Composition rules live in `docs/design-2026-07-25-composition-contract.md` (one clock, two engines; conflicting command-ordering contracts; incompatible spatial models; the ward->site derivation; the region hierarchy ruling). Supporting design history: `docs/design-2026-06-20-murder-loop-survive.md`, `docs/design-2026-06-20-df-feel-depth.md`, `docs/design-2026-07-24-needs-availability-and-condition.md`, `docs/plans/2026-07-24-consume-survival-floor-animal-sim-v2.md`, `docs/brainstorms/2026-08-02-institutional-tier-brainstorm.md`, `docs/brainstorms/2026-08-03-drift-seasons-legibility-brainstorm.md`, `docs/reference-2026-06-30-genre-influences.md`, and the teardowns in `docs/research/` (Dwarf Fortress loops, Heart of the Machine loops). Severity: P0 = would corrupt or block the whole design; P1 = must fix before implementing; P2 = degrades quality; P3 = polish.

SCOPE NOTE FOR THIS LENS. Legibility debt (want D) and adversarial interrogation of the frame (want E) are the primary questions, and the decomposition interrogation (want C) is in scope as an experience model: whether READ/INTEND/COMMIT/RUN/RETURN/ACCRETE describes what a player actually does, or only what the simulation does. Buildability and canon coherence are covered by sibling lenses.
